title: Centre of Mass, Momentum and Collisions
subject: physics

nodes.label: Centre of Mass, Momentum and Collisions
nodes.group: Centre of Mass, Momentum and Collisions
nodes.note: Center of mass, system momentum, conservation laws, the COM frame, and collision dynamics. JEE tests cavity problems, man-boat systems, restitution, and energy loss in collisions.

nodes.label: Centre of Mass Fundamentals
nodes.note: The center of mass is the point where the entire mass can be treated as concentrated for translational motion.

nodes.label: COM Definition
nodes.note: For a system of particles: $$\vec{r}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{1}{M}\sum m_i\vec{r}_i$$. In Cartesian coordinates: $$x_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_i x_i}{M}$$.

nodes.label: Two-Body Lever Rule
nodes.note: For two masses $$m_1$$ and $$m_2$$ separated by distance $$d$$: $$m_1 r_1 = m_2 r_2$$, so $$r_1 = \frac{m_2}{m_1+m_2}d$$. The COM is closer to the heavier mass.

nodes.label: COM vs COG
nodes.note: In a uniform gravitational field, COM and COG coincide. In a non-uniform field, the center of gravity lies slightly below the center of mass.

nodes.label: Continuous Bodies
nodes.note: For continuous mass distributions: $$\vec{r}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{1}{M}\int \vec{r}\,dm$$. Use $$dm = \lambda\,dl$$ for wires, $$\sigma\,dA$$ for laminae, $$\rho\,dV$$ for solids.

nodes.label: Canonical COM Coordinates
nodes.note: Semicircular wire: $$y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{2R}{\pi}$$. Semicircular disc: $$y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{4R}{3\pi}$$. Solid hemisphere: $$y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{3R}{8}$$. Solid cone: $$y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{H}{4}$$.

nodes.label: COM Kinematics
nodes.note: Differentiating the COM position: $$\vec{v}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{d\vec{r}_{\text{cm}}}{dt}$$ and $$\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{d\vec{v}_{\text{cm}}}{dt}$$. The COM moves like a single particle of mass $$M$$.

nodes.label: Negative Mass Method
nodes.note: Bodies with cavities can be solved by superposing the complete body and a negative mass at the cavity.

nodes.label: Superposition Principle
nodes.note: The remaining body is treated as the complete original body plus a negative mass at the cavity: $$\vec{r}_{\text{rem}} = \frac{M_{\text{orig}}\vec{r}_{\text{orig}} - m_{\text{cavity}}\vec{r}_{\text{cavity}}}{M_{\text{orig}} - m_{\text{cavity}}}$$.

nodes.label: Disc with Hole
nodes.note: A disc of radius $$R$$ with a hole of radius $$R/2$$ tangent to the rim: the COM shifts away from the hole by $$x_{\text{cm}} = -\frac{R}{6}$$.

nodes.label: Sphere with Cavity
nodes.note: A sphere of radius $$R$$ with a spherical cavity of radius $$R/2$$ tangent to the surface: the COM shifts by $$x_{\text{cm}} = -\frac{R}{14}$$.

nodes.label: Cavity Principle
nodes.note: The negative mass method works because gravitational and inertial mass are equivalent. The cavity is treated as a region of negative density.

nodes.label: COM Dynamics and Momentum
nodes.note: The center of mass moves as if all mass and external forces were concentrated at that point.

nodes.label: System Momentum
nodes.note: Total momentum equals total mass times COM velocity: $$\vec{P}_{\text{sys}} = \sum m_i\vec{v}_i = M\vec{v}_{\text{cm}}$$.

nodes.label: Newton's Second Law for Systems
nodes.note: Internal forces cancel by Newton's third law: $$\sum \vec{F}_{\text{internal}} = 0$$. Thus $$\vec{F}_{\text{net,ext}} = M\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{d\vec{P}_{\text{sys}}}{dt}$$.

nodes.label: Conservation of Linear Momentum
nodes.note: If net external force is zero, total momentum is conserved: $$\vec{F}_{\text{net,ext}} = 0 \implies \vec{P}_{\text{sys}} = \text{constant}$$.

nodes.label: Directional Conservation
nodes.note: Even with external forces in one direction, momentum is conserved along perpendicular axes. If $$F_{\text{ext},x} = 0$$, then $$P_{x,\text{sys}} = \text{constant}$$.

nodes.label: Relative Displacement Mechanics
nodes.note: For a system initially at rest with zero external force, $$\Delta \vec{r}_{\text{cm}} = 0 \iff \sum m_i \Delta\vec{r}_i = 0$$.

nodes.label: Man on Boat
nodes.note: A man of mass $$m$$ walks distance $$L$$ on a boat of mass $$M$$: the boat shifts back by $$x_{\text{boat}} = \frac{m}{M+m}L$$ and the man's ground displacement is $$\frac{M}{M+m}L$$.

nodes.label: Explosion Trajectory Invariance
nodes.note: A projectile exploding mid-flight: internal forces do not affect the COM. The center of mass continues along the original parabolic trajectory until the first fragment lands.

nodes.label: Internal Force Annihilation
nodes.note: Internal forces occur in action-reaction pairs that cancel: $$\sum \vec{F}_{\text{internal}} = 0$$. Only external forces affect the COM motion.

nodes.label: Centre of Mass Frame
nodes.note: The zero-momentum frame simplifies two-body problems and collision analysis.

nodes.label: C-Frame Properties
nodes.note: In the COM frame, total momentum is identically zero: $$\sum m_i\vec{v}_i^* = 0$$. For two bodies, $$\vec{p}_1^* = -\vec{p}_2^*$$.

nodes.label: Reduced Mass
nodes.note: The reduced mass is $$\mu = \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$$. It transforms a two-body problem into an equivalent one-body problem.

nodes.label: Coupled Spring Oscillator
nodes.note: Two masses connected by a spring of stiffness $$k$$: the relative motion is SHM with $$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}}$$ and $$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{k}}$$.

nodes.label: Maximum Spring Compression
nodes.note: Maximum compression occurs when relative velocity is zero: $$\frac{1}{2}kx_{\max}^2 = \frac{1}{2}\mu v_{\text{rel},0}^2$$, so $$x_{\max} = v_0\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{k}}$$.

nodes.label: Konig's Theorem
nodes.note: Total kinetic energy decomposes: $$K_{\text{lab}} = \frac{1}{2}Mv_{\text{cm}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\mu v_{\text{rel}}^2$$. The translational part is frozen when $$\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0$$.

nodes.label: Collisions in C-Frame
nodes.note: In the COM frame, the two colliding bodies approach and recede along the same line. The C-frame simplifies restitution analysis.

nodes.label: Collisions
nodes.note: Impulse, coefficient of restitution, head-on collisions, energy loss, and oblique scattering.

nodes.label: Impulse-Momentum Theorem
nodes.note: Impulse equals change in momentum: $$\vec{J} = \int \vec{F}\,dt = \Delta\vec{P}$$. Impulsive forces are large but brief; non-impulsive forces like gravity are negligible during impact.

nodes.label: Coefficient of Restitution
nodes.note: Newton's experimental law: $$e = \frac{v_{\text{sep}}}{u_{\text{app}}}$$ along the line of impact. $$e = 1$$ is elastic; $$e = 0$$ is perfectly inelastic.

nodes.label: Head-On 1D Collisions
nodes.note: For masses $$m_1, m_2$$ with initial velocities $$u_1, u_2$$: $$v_1 = \frac{m_1 - em_2}{m_1+m_2}u_1 + \frac{(1+e)m_2}{m_1+m_2}u_2$$ and $$v_2 = \frac{(1+e)m_1}{m_1+m_2}u_1 + \frac{m_2 - em_1}{m_1+m_2}u_2$$.

nodes.label: Equal Mass Elastic
nodes.note: For $$m_1 = m_2$$ and $$e = 1$$: the bodies exchange velocities, $$v_1 = u_2$$ and $$v_2 = u_1$$.

nodes.label: Massive Stationary Target
nodes.note: For $$m_2 \gg m_1$$ and $$u_2 = 0$$: the light particle rebounds with $$v_1 \approx -eu_1$$. For a massive striker on a light target: $$v_2 \approx (1+e)u_1$$.

nodes.label: Kinetic Energy Loss
nodes.note: The universal energy loss formula is $$\Delta K = \frac{1}{2}\mu(1-e^2)u_{\text{rel}}^2$$. Maximum loss occurs for perfectly inelastic collisions ($$e = 0$$).

nodes.label: Bouncing Ball Series
nodes.note: A ball dropped from height $$h_0$$ with restitution $$e$$: after $$n$$ bounces, $$h_n = e^{2n}h_0$$. Total distance is $$H_{\text{total}} = h_0\frac{1+e^2}{1-e^2}$$.

nodes.label: Oblique Collisions
nodes.note: In 2D collisions, tangential velocity components are unchanged. Along the line of impact, momentum is conserved and restitution applies.

nodes.label: 90-Degree Scattering Theorem
nodes.note: For equal masses with one stationary and $$e = 1$$: the two particles fly off at right angles, $$\theta_1 + \theta_2 = 90^\circ$$.

nodes.label: Ballistic Pendulum
nodes.note: A bullet embedding in a pendulum bob is perfectly inelastic ($$e = 0$$). Momentum is conserved during impact; mechanical energy is conserved during the swing.

nodes.label: Variable Mass Systems
nodes.note: For a body ejecting mass: $$m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} + \vec{v}_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}$$. The thrust force is $$\vec{F}_{\text{thrust}} = \vec{v}_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}$$.

nodes.label: Rocket Equation
nodes.note: In gravity-free space: $$v(t) = v_0 + u_{\text{ex}}\ln\frac{m_0}{m}$$. In uniform gravity: $$v(t) = v_0 - gt + u_{\text{ex}}\ln\frac{m_0}{m}$$.
